conceptTag: Should you sign an exclusive deal?
readerTitle: The grocery chain wants you all to itself. Do you say yes?
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (식품 회사 안의 신제품 팀 × 지역 식료품 체인) · 모든 상황과 수치는 설명용
insight: 독점은 '예/아니오'가 아니라 범위, 기간, 대가, 종료 조건을 하나하나 정해 값을 매기는 거래다.
misconception: 큰 유통사가 독점을 원하면 우리 제품을 그만큼 밀어 줄 테니 그대로 받는 게 이득이다.

sources.text: 모든 상황과 수치는 설명용 가상 시뮬레이션
협상·제휴 실무의 일반 원칙 (독점의 범위·기간·성과 조건)

factChecks.note: 60개 매장, 12개월, 2개 분기 연속 미달 등 모든 수치는 가상입니다. 실제 통계나 기업 사례를 인용하지 않았습니다.
8번 카드의 경쟁법 언급은 '일부 시장에서 문제가 될 수 있으니 전문가와 확인'이라는 일반론으로만 적었습니다. 특정 국가의 법률 조언이 되지 않도록 게시 전 문구를 다시 확인하세요.

cards.title: The grocery chain wants you all to itself. Do you say yes?
body: You lead a small new-products team inside a mid-sized food company. Your team just launched a line of baked lentil chips.
A regional grocery chain with 60 stores loves them. The buyer has one condition: *nobody else in the region gets to sell them.* Four decisions follow. Make each one before reading on.

image.label: A grocery buyer sliding a contract across a table next to a bag of chips
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 식료품 체인 바이어가 테이블 너머로 계약서를 밀고, 앞에 렌틸 칩 봉지 하나. 계약서에 큰 글씨로 "Exclusive". 실제 브랜드 로고나 매장 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: The buyer offers exclusivity. Your first move?
body: The chain would put your chips in all 60 stores. In return, you'd sell them nowhere else in the region.

options.text: Sign. Sixty stores is a great start
options.feedback: You get shelf space fast but give away every other store in the region for nothing specific in return. If the chain loses interest, you're stuck.

options.text: Decline. Never limit where you sell
options.feedback: You keep every option open but may lose the one partner ready to push a new product hard. Exclusivity has value, so it can be traded.

options.text: Counter: ask what the chain commits in return
options.feedback: Exclusivity is something you give up, so it should buy something. You ask for minimum orders and eye-level shelf space in every store.

cards.title: Say you countered. Now, how wide is "exclusive"?
body: The chain agrees to minimum orders and good shelf spots. Its draft says exclusive for three years, all your products, every channel, nationwide.

options.text: Accept. They gave you what you asked for
options.feedback: You'd block future products, online sales and other regions for three years. The chain only operates in one region.

options.text: Narrow it: this chip line, this region, physical stores, 12 months with renewal
options.feedback: The chain gets real protection where it competes. You keep everything else, and you can review the deal after a year.

options.text: Offer a 3-month head start instead of exclusivity
options.feedback: Safer for you, but the chain may not invest in a product it will soon share. You might lose the shelf push you wanted.

cards.title: Say you narrowed it. What if sales stall?
body: The buyer promises a big launch. But buyers change jobs, and shelves get rearranged.

options.text: Trust the relationship. Clauses signal distrust
options.feedback: It keeps the mood warm today. If the chain stops pushing, you're locked out of other stores for the rest of the term.

options.text: Add a penalty fee if orders fall short
options.feedback: It gives the chain a reason to order, but fees cause fights and don't free you to sell elsewhere.

options.text: Exclusivity ends automatically if minimums are missed for two quarters in a row
options.feedback: The chain keeps exclusivity only while it earns it. If it doesn't, you're free without a dispute.

cards.title: Say you added the trigger. One last check.
body: The deal is ready. Then a colleague mentions that your company's food-service team is talking to a rival chain's café business about snacks.

options.text: Sign now. Their talks are their problem
options.feedback: You close fast, but your contract may block a deal your own company wants. Inside a larger company, your exclusivity is everyone's exclusivity.

options.text: Share the draft with other teams and get sign-off on what it blocks
options.feedback: It costs a week. You learn the café deal is fine because it's a different channel, and you write that carve-out into the contract.

options.text: Drop the deal to avoid internal conflict
options.feedback: No internal friction, but you give up a good partner over a question one meeting could answer.

cards.title: A year later, the clauses did the work.
body: Sales were strong for two quarters. Then the buyer left, and the chips moved to a bottom shelf. Orders fell below the minimum twice in a row.
Exclusivity ended on its own. You signed a second chain within a month, while the first kept selling the chips without exclusivity. No lawyers, no fight.

image.label: Timeline: strong sales, buyer leaves, trigger ends exclusivity, second chain signs
image.brief: 가로 타임라인 인포그래픽. 1~2분기 높은 막대, 3~4분기 점선(최소 주문량) 아래로 떨어진 막대, 그 지점에 "Exclusivity ends" 깃발, 이어서 두 번째 매장 아이콘 등장. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Exclusivity is a price, not a prize.
body: **Exclusivity** means you give up selling to others so one partner can stand out. What you give up is real: every store, channel and product you can't reach.
So treat it like anything you sell. Decide what it covers, how long it lasts, what you get in return, and when it stops. A deal that names all four is one you can live with when things change.

cards.title: Clauses don't create effort.
body: A trigger frees you when sales fall, but it can't make a partner care. Narrow exclusivity also gives the partner less reason to invest, so expect some trade-off.
In some markets, exclusive deals by large firms can raise competition-law questions. Check with a lawyer before signing anything broad.

cards.title: Give exclusivity in slices, and make each slice earn its keep.
list: **Decision 1, ask for something back:** exclusivity has value (SAL-07-05)
**Decision 2, narrow the scope:** cover only where the partner competes
**Decision 3, add a trigger:** keep both sides' incentives tied to results (SAL-07-03), with a clean exit (SAL-07-06)
**Decision 4, check inside first:** your deal can block your own company's options
cards.callout: **Try it today:** take one partner deal you have or want. Write its scope, term, payment in return and exit condition on one line each.
cards.softwareNote: The same four questions apply when a reseller or app marketplace asks to be your only channel in a country. Limit it to that market, set a sales threshold, and let it lapse if the threshold is missed.
